text: Co-packaged optics (CPO) reduces interconnect energy mainly by:
choices: Shortening the electrical path from ~100 mm faceplate traces (~1 pJ/bit SerDes) to ~1 mm package traces (~100 fJ/bit)
Cooling the transceiver laser to cryogenic temperatures
Replacing photons with electrons in the link
Raising the supply voltage to drive longer traces
explanation: CPO moves the optical engine next to the switch ASIC, collapsing the energy-hungry electrical SerDes path from ~100 mm to ~1 mm and cutting that dominant component about 10x. It does not use cryogenics, keeps photons for transport, and raising voltage would increase (not reduce) energy.
